bib.title: Chapter 6. Statistical Machine Learning (Practical Statistics for Data Scientists)

question: How do KNN, decision trees, bagging/random forests and boosting work, and how do you keep them from overfitting?

limits: All numbers are single illustrative runs on Lending Club data with no seeds, repeats or intervals.
Code uses R (FNN, rpart, randomForest, xgboost); ntreelimit and the knn syntax are older xgboost/FNN versions.
Equations (Euclidean, Gini, entropy, bagged estimate, Adaboost, ridge, lasso) are images and are missing from the extracted text.
Published 2017: no gradient-boosting variants such as LightGBM or CatBoost.
practices: Standardize predictors before KNN, PCA or clustering so large-scale variables do not dominate distance (Standardization).
Choose K by accuracy on holdout/validation data; low K overfits, high K oversmooths; typically K 1-20, odd to avoid ties (Choosing K).
Use KNN probabilities with a cutoff below 0.5 for rare classes (KNN note).
Use KNN output as a feature for a second-stage model (KNN as a Feature Engine).
Prune trees or set cp by repeated train/validation partitioning; try a few cp values in exploration (Stopping the Tree from Growing).
Prefer permutation (out-of-bag accuracy decrease) variable importance over Gini decrease, which is training-based and less reliable (Variable Importance).
Tune random forest nodesize and maxnodes by cross-validation to avoid overfitting noisy data (Hyperparameters).
For XGBoost use small eta (0.1) with more rounds, shallow trees, subsample/colsample, and lambda/alpha regularization; tune by cross-validation (XGBoost, Hyperparameters and Cross-Validation).
Omit one dummy in linear/logistic regression after one-hot encoding; not needed for KNN and trees (One Hot Encoder).

terms.definition: Variance refers to the modeling error that occurs because of the choice of training data; bias refers to the modeling error that occurs because you have not properly identified the underlying real-world scenario; this error would not disappear if you simply added more training data.
parameters that you need to set before fitting a model; they are not optimized as part of the training process
A general technique to form a collection of models by bootstrapping the data.
bagging applied to decision trees that also samples variables at each split; rule of thumb p=sqrt(P) (formula image missing)
A general technique to fit a sequence of models by giving more weight to the records with large residuals for each successive round.
the error rate for the trained models, applied to the data left out of the training set for that tree
A technique to avoid overfitting by adding a penalty term to the cost function on the number of parameters in the model.
The extent to which a mix of classes is found in a subpartition of the data (the more mixed, the more impure).
The process of taking a fully grown tree and progressively cutting its branches back, to reduce overfitting.
randomly splits up the data into K different groups (folds); a model is trained on data not in the fold and evaluated on the fold; best hyperparameters have lowest average error
